In summary, our research is concerned with

the following contributions: (a) we provide a uniform framework for studying different combinations of rules and ontological knowledge; (b) we show how to represent the combinations as FO-AEL theories; (c) we show how the combination properties are reflected in the FO-AEL theories, and (d) we show how our results can be used to compare the combination types.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the embedding of a combination approach into AEL is not necessarily a trivial exercise and that the choice of an embedding may influence the properties of the resulting combination approach.
the combination of rules and ontology languages in the context of autoepistemic semantics leads to a variety of interesting and complex formalisms.
the embeddings of dl-programs and r-hybrid knowledgebases are very close to each other, while the embedding of hybrid MKNF is more complicated, but still possible.

the embeddings can be used to study the different combination formalisms in a common framework.
